mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 7% within a month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 7% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE crosses above 7% in a single month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which depresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO below its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) over two consecutive months signals broad-based demand contraction, which reduces corporate revenue and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A low and stable federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 1% for at least six months) combined with rising consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 2%) signals accommodative monetary policy in an inflationary environment, which supports equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% for 6 months AND CPIAUCSL YoY > 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS < 1% for six months and CPIAUCSL YoY > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average for 5 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS is above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months, alongside a decline in consumer spending (GDPC1), signals a shift from consumption to saving, which typically precedes a future economic slowdown and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for 3 months AND GDPC1 falls
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is above its 12-month moving average for three months and GDPC1 falls.
